guidance.evidence_criterion: Read the complete definition together with every route by which information becomes confidential and any operative confidentiality duty. For explicit identification, support requires a marking, designation, or confirmation regime applicable to the covered disclosures; oppose when confidentiality can instead arise from nature, context, reasonable understanding, or unmarked categorical inclusion. A mixed rule with an identification route and an alternative context-based route opposes an assertion that all information must be expressly identified. For technical-only scope, oppose whenever any non-technical category is expressly included; do not infer technical-only status from examples or silence. For oral information, support only when oral or verbal disclosure is covered directly or through a confirmation procedure; broad references to information, generated material, or communications alone do not establish oral coverage. For confidentiality of the agreement or its negotiation, require language covering the existence, terms, negotiations, communications, or contractual arrangements of this agreement plus an applicable confidentiality obligation; discussions about a different prospective relationship do not suffice. Use NotMentioned when the exact form or subject is unsettled. Cite all definition branches and operative provisions necessary to establish the boundary, including independently annotated categories, but not unrelated examples.

Separate the two acquisition routes. Independent development concerns creation by the receiving party without use of, access to, reference to, or reliance on protected information. Third-party acquisition concerns receipt from a person entitled to disclose and not bound by confidentiality. An exclusion from the definition or confidentiality obligations can support the corresponding permission even if phrased as an exception rather than an affirmative grant. Do not use third-party receipt to support independent development or vice versa, and do not infer either route from a general public-domain or prior-possession exception. Support when the matching route is expressly available, oppose when it is expressly forbidden, and otherwise return NotMentioned. Cite the exception lead-in when it supplies the legal effect and every matching condition needed to show the route and its limits.

Identify the receiving actor, the expressly permitted recipient class, the information disclosed, and every need-to-know, purpose, approval, or confidentiality condition. Employee sharing is supported only by a clause authorizing access or disclosure to employees; third-party sharing is supported by an affirmative permitted class such as agents, representatives, consultants, advisers, or other non-employees. A permission limited to employees does not support third-party sharing. A general nondisclosure rule that never addresses the relevant class is unresolved, while an exclusive recipient list that omits the class, an express prohibition, or a regime allowing outsiders only through case-specific discloser approval opposes a standing permission. Do not treat responsibility for a recipient's breach as itself permission to disclose. Cite the operative permission or exclusion, its recipient class, and all provisions imposing necessary conditions; include separately operative recipient provisions when independently relevant.

Analyze return or destruction, creation of copies, and post-disposition retention as separate actions. A termination-based return/destruction statement is supported only when termination, expiration, or failure to consummate the contemplated arrangement itself activates the duty; a demand-only duty, or a termination clause effective only if a later request is made, does not establish that proposition. For copying, require an affirmative right to reproduce or copy in identified circumstances. A prohibition on copying, including one liftable only by case-specific consent, opposes that permission; a right to retain an existing archival copy or a command to return copies does not prove a right to create one. Post-disposition possession is supported only by an express archival, legal-compliance, backup, infeasibility, or similar retention carveout that operates after the return/destruction obligation. An exhaustive duty covering all materials and copies with no carveout opposes retention; silence is unresolved. Cite the trigger, operative action, covered objects, and each exception or qualification that changes the result, excluding merely contextual disposition language not part of the original decision boundary.

Match the exact actor, action, and object rather than treating all restrictive clauses alike. Limited use is supported by a sole-purpose authorization or an express ban on every other purpose; resolve any defined purpose and cite it when needed, together with all independently operative use restrictions. No licensing is supported by language denying licenses, title, interests, or other rights in the protected information; ownership language and a no-grant clause should both be cited when they jointly state the rule. A reference preserving rights under a separate agreement does not itself mean this NDA grants them. Oppose only if this agreement affirmatively grants the relevant right. Reverse engineering requires language specifically prohibiting or permitting reverse engineering, decompilation, disassembly, or an equivalent examination of objects embodying the information. Do not infer it from limited-use, nondisclosure, ownership, no-license, copying, or general security provisions. If the exact action is not settled, return NotMentioned.

Locate a legally compelled disclosure trigger and determine whether the receiving party must communicate with the disclosing party before or promptly upon disclosure. Notice, advance consultation, or a required opportunity to contest can support the duty even without the word 'notify'; cooperation or disclosure-limitation language alone cannot. A compelled-disclosure exception with no communication duty is unresolved, and an express authorization to disclose without notice opposes. Cite the operative communication duty and include its lead-in only when needed to establish that the duty applies to protected information compelled by law, regulation, court, or governmental process. Include separate contest or timing language only when it is part of the annotated duty.

Determine whether any contractual obligation, rather than merely a right or factual condition, continues after termination or expiration. Support an express survival sentence, a fixed post-termination duration, or language stating that confidentiality or non-use continues. If the survival clause names or cross-references particular sections, inspect those sections and cite the operative obligations together with the survival language; if a broad survival clause is self-contained, cite that clause without importing unrelated provisions. Do not infer survival merely because the agreement has a term, permits later retention, or lacks a termination release. Oppose an express termination of all obligations; otherwise use NotMentioned when post-termination effect is unstated.

Require an operative restriction on the receiving party soliciting, enticing, inducing, recruiting, or hiring identified employees or other representatives of the disclosing party. Verify the protected class, prohibited conduct, purpose, duration, and any consent exception. A restriction on contacting information sources, disclosing names, using confidential information, or communicating with representatives is not a nonsolicitation covenant unless it addresses solicitation or equivalent recruitment conduct. Support an applicable prohibition, oppose an express permission to solicit, and otherwise return NotMentioned. Cite the complete operative covenant and any clause defining its protected class or material exception.

Read the complete definition, every alternative route into confidentiality, and the operative restriction. For explicit identification, support only when all covered disclosures are subject to the document's marking, designation, oral-identification, or confirmation regime; oppose when a broad category, reasonable-understanding rule, or unmarked/contextual route independently creates protection. Do not treat the mere naming of information categories as identification. For technical-only scope, oppose when any business, financial, personnel, contractual, commercial, or other non-technical category is included; silence about categories is unresolved. For oral information, require express coverage of oral, verbal, visual, or observed disclosure, or an oral-disclosure confirmation procedure; do not infer oral coverage from generic references to information, meetings, communications, or substantive examples. For confidentiality of the agreement or negotiations, support an operative restriction covering this agreement's existence, contents, terms, negotiations, discussions, or communications; a direct ban on public announcement of the agreement's contents qualifies even if those contents are not separately defined as Confidential Information. Discussions concerning a different prospective relationship do not suffice. Cite every independently annotated definition branch and operative provision needed for the result, including terminal form-of-disclosure language that governs a preceding list.

operations.rationale: The current lawyer omitted direct agreement-content restrictions in cases 147 and 319 and repeatedly inferred oral coverage from generic categories in cases 314, 167, and 545. Case 390 confirms that an express oral-form clause supports oral coverage. The update tightens the form and subject checks while preserving the existing identification and technical-scope boundaries.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Separate creation from acquisition and identify who performs the relevant act. Independent development requires an express route under which the receiving party creates or develops similar information without use of, access to, reference to, or reliance on protected information. A general definition, permitted use outside a business, public-domain exception, legal-disclosure exception, prior possession, or mere absence of a development ban does not establish that route. Third-party acquisition requires the receiving party to obtain information from a third party entitled to disclose it and free of the relevant confidentiality restriction. Do not confuse this with the disclosing party's disclosure to a third party, a written-consent exception, or permission for the receiving party to disclose outward. An exclusion from the definition or confidentiality duties can support the matching route when its lead-in supplies that legal effect. Otherwise use NotMentioned unless the matching conduct is expressly forbidden. Cite the exception lead-in and all conditions necessary to identify the actor, route, and freedom from restriction.

operations.rationale: Cases 134, 545, and 390 show false independent-development findings from broad definitions, use carveouts, or unrelated exceptions. Cases 384 and 188 show false third-party-acquisition findings where the text instead addressed consent or disclosure by the discloser, while case 319 shows the need to capture the complete matching exception.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Identify the receiving actor, the recipient class, the disclosed information, and every need-to-know, purpose, approval, notice, or confidentiality condition. Employee sharing is supported only by an operative authorization of employee access or disclosure. Third-party sharing is supported by an affirmative standing permission covering at least one non-employee class, such as agents, representatives, consultants, advisers, directors acting outside an employee-only class, or another specified outsider. Read exceptions as controlling over a general nondisclosure rule: a clause allowing employees and agents can support third-party sharing despite an earlier general ban. Conversely, an employee-only exclusive list, an express outsider prohibition, or disclosure available only after case-specific approval does not establish a standing third-party permission and may oppose it when the regime exhaustively addresses permitted recipients. Responsibility for another person's breach, access granted for a role, or a reference to unauthorized persons is not itself permission. Cite the operative permission or prohibition plus all independently operative provisions defining the class and its conditions; do not substitute a general indemnity or authorized-user reference for the actual access clause.

operations.rationale: The lawyer treated case-specific approval as permission in case 147, missed exclusive employee-only opposition in cases 314 and 328, missed agents or representatives in cases 149 and 390, and used non-operative recipient evidence in case 89. Cases 545 and 188 reinforce that a general reference to outsiders does not itself authorize sharing.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Analyze the trigger, disposition action, copying action, and retained object separately. A termination-based return or destruction duty is supported only when termination, expiration, failure to consummate, or an equivalent end event itself activates the duty. A demand-only duty, or a termination clause requiring an additional request, does not suffice. For copying, require an affirmative standing right to make copies in identified circumstances. A prohibition subject only to case-specific consent opposes that permission; permission to retain an existing copy and commands concerning copies do not prove a right to create one. Post-disposition possession is supported only by an express archival, compliance, backup, infeasibility, or comparable retention carveout operating notwithstanding the return or destruction duty. Oppose when the applicable provision exhaustively requires return or destruction of all information, originals, copies, reproductions, derivatives, or other embodiments without a retention carveout; this can oppose retention even when disposition is demand-triggered. Cite the complete trigger and operative duty, all annotated covered-object language, certifications that establish no retention, and every exception that changes the result. Do not cite contextual disposition language that neither governs nor qualifies the action.

operations.rationale: Cases 617, 149, and 319 show that demand language was wrongly treated as termination-triggered. Cases 147, 167, 134, 319, and 426 show missed opposition from exhaustive no-retention duties, while cases 328, 384, and 89 distinguish complete destruction rules from an express infeasibility carveout. Case 147 also shows that consent-liftable copying prohibitions are not affirmative copy rights.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Match the exact actor, action, and object. Limited use is supported by a sole-purpose authorization or an express prohibition on other uses; resolve any defined purpose and cite each independently operative use restriction or exception needed to state its scope. No licensing is supported by an express denial of licenses, title, interests, or other rights, or by an operative reservation stating that ownership or title in the protected information and its copies remains exclusively with the discloser. Cite both ownership and no-grant provisions when both independently state the annotated rule. Permission to receive, access, evaluate, use, or disclose information for a limited role is not an affirmative grant of a proprietary right and therefore does not oppose no-licensing. Oppose only when this agreement affirmatively vests or grants the relevant right; a separate-agreement exception does not itself make the grant. Reverse engineering requires an express prohibition or permission concerning reverse engineering, decompilation, disassembly, or equivalent examination of an object embodying the information. Do not infer it from use limits, nondisclosure, ownership, copying, security, or no-license language. If the exact conduct is unsettled, use NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: Case 319 shows that an operative reservation of title can establish no rights even without a separate no-license sentence. Cases 285, 426, and 390 show false contradictions caused by confusing access, role, or unrelated waiver language with an affirmative rights grant. Cases 617, 147, and 314 support complete citation of independently operative ownership and no-grant provisions.

guidance.evidence_criterion: Determine whether any contractual duty continues beyond termination, expiration, completion of the stated purpose, or another event ending the operative relationship. Support an express survival sentence, a fixed post-ending duration, or language stating that confidentiality, non-use, or another obligation continues after that event. A provision making the agreement binding during the purpose and for an additional period after the purpose is completed can establish survival even without the word 'termination.' By contrast, a clause merely setting the agreement's ordinary term from execution or disclosure does not establish that obligations survive termination. If survival names or cross-references particular sections, inspect and cite the operative obligations together with the survival language; if a broad survival clause is self-contained, do not import unrelated provisions. Retention permission, continuing facts, and silence do not establish survival. Oppose an express termination of all obligations; otherwise use NotMentioned.

operations.rationale: The lawyer incorrectly treated the ordinary five-year agreement term in case 207 as survival and missed the express continuation beyond completion of the purpose in case 134. Cases 617 and 89 also show when cross-referenced operative duties must accompany survival language for complete evidence.
